papers.title: Influence of Cell Type, Label Type, and Recovery Times on In-Cell Pulsed Dipolar Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Spectroscopy Data
papers.authors: Yannik Limbach, Philipp Schult, Katrin Paeschke, Bela E. Bode, Olav Schiemann
papers.summary: Pulsed dipolar EPR compares trityl and gadolinium labels in several cell environments. Label concentration, cell type and recovery time alter binding, modulation depth and the preservation of distance information.
papers.whyRelevant: Highlights environmental and sample-preparation effects that can bias radical-based sensing readouts.

relatedPapers.reason: Both involve organic radical spins and their response to surrounding environments.

papers.title: Enhanced quantum sensing mediated by a cavity in open systems
papers.authors: Quinn Langfitt, Zain Saleem, Michael A Perlin, Tian Zhong, A Shaji, Stephen K Gray
papers.summary: Open-system simulations compare probe states for sensing with cavity-coupled qubits. Within the simulated system sizes, the preferred state and precision scaling depend strongly on the balance between coupling and dissipation.
papers.whyRelevant: Useful theoretical context for deciding whether collective correlations remain beneficial under realistic losses.

relatedPapers.reason: Both concern extracting environmental information from quantum spin dynamics, using different platforms.

papers.title: Spin controlled transport switching with negative differential resistance in a chiral molecular device
papers.summary: The study links crystal-field and oxidation-state control to spin-dependent transport in a chiral molecular junction. Orbital alignment and asymmetric ligand coupling are associated with switching, rectification and negative differential resistance.
papers.whyRelevant: A molecular-device perspective on how local spin states and contacts jointly affect transport.

relatedPapers.reason: Contact engineering and the relationship between molecular structure and electrical response are shared themes.

papers.title: Magnetic-field-orientation-controlled spin-dependent charge transport in organic magnetic transistors
papers.authors: Po-Hsiang Fang, Shan-Jui Hsu, Jrjeng Ruan, Horng-Long Cheng, Wei-Yang Chou
papers.summary: Magnetite nanoparticles embedded in a conjugated-polymer transistor produce orientation-dependent magnetic transport. Electrical and spectroscopic measurements associate the response with interfacial magnetic interactions, molecular packing and spin-dependent carrier scattering.
papers.whyRelevant: Relevant to distinguishing contact, morphology and spin effects when interpreting organic-device magnetoresistance.

relatedPapers.reason: Both address device interfaces and carrier transport in sensitive molecular materials.

papers.title: Pores and Polymers: Metal–Organic Framework and Polymer Composite Materials
papers.summary: This Account compares mixed-matrix membranes, polymer-grafted MOF monolayers and polymer-linked frameworks. It explains trade-offs between pore accessibility, mechanical robustness and the ability to process crystalline frameworks into usable forms.
papers.whyRelevant: A synthesis-to-integration overview for bringing fragile framework materials into films and devices.

relatedPapers.reason: Both consider interfaces between molecular or framework components and polymers.

papers.title: Molecular Curvature Enables Tubular π-Stacked Pathways in Three-Dimensional Conductive Metal-Organic Frameworks
papers.authors: Weishan Li, Jia-Xiang Zhang, Tongyang Zhao, Hao Chen, Tianyang Chen, Ze-Fan Yao, Jin-Hu Dou
papers.summary: Twisted ligands organize lanthanide MOFs into three-dimensional structures containing tubular aromatic stacks. Single-crystal characterization and transport measurements link this architecture to mixed electron–proton conduction, with metal substitution tuning stacking and pore environments.
papers.whyRelevant: Closely matches the group’s interest in ligand packing, single-crystal structure and conductive-framework transport.

relatedPapers.reason: Closely matches the group’s interest in ligand packing, single-crystal structure and conductive-framework transport.

papers.title: Dynamical-mean-field cluster-correlation expansion of NV$^-$ spin-echo decoherence in a realistic substitutional-nitrogen bath
papers.summary: A dynamical mean-field extension of cluster-correlation expansion treats correlated bath-spin flip-flops during NV spin echo. It reduces discrepancies associated with a frozen bath without invoking extra dark defects, although low-field disagreement with experiment remains.
papers.whyRelevant: A directly relevant modeling reference for spin-bath contributions to coherence in dense molecular-qubit materials.

relatedPapers.reason: A directly relevant modeling reference for spin-bath contributions to coherence in dense molecular-qubit materials.

papers.title: Stacked-Ring Aromaticity Rewires Quantum Interference and Through-Space Transport
papers.authors: Kenan Uriostegui, Flor María Briceño-Vargas, Jessica Arcudia, François Leyvraz, Filiberto Ortiz-Chi, Thomas Stegmann, Mesías Orozco-Ic
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.archiveJournal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: A theoretical analysis shows how cofacial stacking of antiaromatic molecules reorganizes quantum interference and through-space transport. Layer coupling can reverse which electrode connectivity favors conduction, linking stacking geometry with the molecular-junction response.
papers.whyRelevant: Closely relevant to the relationship between aromatic stacking and charge transport in conducting frameworks.

relatedPapers.reason: Closely relevant to the relationship between aromatic stacking and charge transport in conducting frameworks.

papers.title: Interfacial Kinetic Control Enables Regulated Growth of Functional Metal–Phenolic Network Films
papers.authors: Tianzheng Wang, Zhixing Lin, Omid Mazaheri, Chang Liu, Wanjun Xu, Zhaoran Wang, Jingqu Chen, Ben McLean, Irene Yarovsky, Ali Zavabeti, Joseph J. Richardson, Frank Caruso
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.archiveJournal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: Liquid–liquid interfacial assembly regulates growth of metal–phenolic network films and broadens the available building blocks. The approach controls film thickness and mechanical properties and supports incorporation of conductive or optically functional components.
papers.whyRelevant: A useful synthesis route for controlling functional framework films and their interfaces.

relatedPapers.reason: A useful synthesis route for controlling functional framework films and their interfaces.

papers.title: Quartet state of the neutral nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond and optimized spin readout under near-infrared two-photon excitation
papers.authors: Nikoletta Jegenyes, Pál Maák, Vladimir Verkhovlyuk, László Himics, Tamás Váczi, Miklós Veres, Ádám Gali
papers.summary: Two-photon ODMR locates a metastable neutral-NV quartet through an excitation threshold. The identified near-infrared excitation window improves spin-readout sensitivity relative to the comparison wavelengths measured in the same setup.
papers.whyRelevant: An optical-readout design reference for luminescent spin systems; the demonstrated mechanism is specific to diamond defects.

relatedPapers.reason: An optical-readout design reference for luminescent spin systems; the demonstrated mechanism is specific to diamond defects.

papers.title: Theoretical investigation of switching molecular Kondo effect via atomic-scale hydrogen control
papers.authors: Yushan Wang, Xiaoguang Li, Yu Wang
papers.summary: First-principles calculations predict hydrogen-controlled changes in the magnetic state of cobalt phthalocyanine on gold. Hydrogenation alters molecular geometry, substrate coupling and charge distribution, suggesting a mechanism for switching a molecular Kondo response.
papers.whyRelevant: Directly relevant to substrate effects and chemical manipulation of individual molecular spins; the reported study is theoretical.

relatedPapers.reason: Directly relevant to substrate effects and chemical manipulation of individual molecular spins; the reported study is theoretical.

papers.title: The effects of an alternating bias on a single orbital spin impurity
papers.authors: Matyas Nachtigall, Jose Reina-Gálvez, Christoph Wolf, Nicolás Lorente
papers.summary: A quantum-master-equation treatment inserts an oscillating STM bias through electronic reservoirs. The analysis distinguishes charge-transfer and exchange-field torques, showing how RF amplitude changes both the effective spin drive and the sampled transport regime.
papers.whyRelevant: Closely related to coherent addressing of individual molecular spins and the interpretation of electrically driven resonance.

relatedPapers.reason: Closely related to coherent addressing of individual molecular spins and the interpretation of electrically driven resonance.

papers.title: Guest-Programmed Adaptive Redistribution in Heteroleptic Metal–Organic Cages
papers.authors: Wei-Jie Zhang, Yi-Lin Pan, Wen-Hui Bi, Tanya K. Ronson, Laura Schneider, Guido H. Clever, Mladen Vinković, Quentin Duez, Cheng-Yong Su, Jonathan R. Nitschke, Kai Wu
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.archiveJournal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: Guest recognition shifts the distribution of heteroleptic zinc cages through coupled reassembly equilibria. Crystallographic and computational analyses identify noncovalent interactions associated with selectivity, while guest binding also changes luminescence.
papers.whyRelevant: Relevant to programmable host–guest environments and the structural adaptability of functional coordination assemblies.

relatedPapers.reason: Relevant to programmable host–guest environments and the structural adaptability of functional coordination assemblies.

papers.title: Ultralow frequency magnetic comb using pulse modulated spin maser
papers.authors: Weiyu Wang, Qingchang Li, Erwei Li, Lan Wu, Qianjin Ma, Shougang Zhang, Guobin Liu
papers.summary: A pulse-modulated rubidium–xenon spin maser produces an ultralow-frequency magnetic comb. Pulse duration and feedback strength and phase shape its spectrum, while a spin-echo-chain model gives preliminary agreement with the measurements.
papers.whyRelevant: A cross-platform example of pulse and feedback engineering for magnetic-resonance measurements.

relatedPapers.reason: A cross-platform example of pulse and feedback engineering for magnetic-resonance measurements.

papers.title: Dual Lanthanide (Eu–Tb) Doped 2D MOFs with Tunable Multicolor Emission for Fluorescence Sensing
papers.authors: Yi-Ying Wang, Hai-Qing Zhou, Ya Gao, Xiao-Li Hu, Tan Su, Zhong-Min Su
papers.summary: Two related lanthanide MOFs show analyte-dependent fluorescence responses, while mixed europium–terbium compositions enable ratiometric and visual detection. The study combines aqueous stability tests with investigations of possible quenching mechanisms.
papers.whyRelevant: An optical chemical-sensing comparison for framework-hosted recognition; no spin-based quantum advantage is claimed.

relatedPapers.reason: An optical chemical-sensing comparison for framework-hosted recognition; no spin-based quantum advantage is claimed.
